open_points.subject: A21 formal invariant and Required test 2
open_points.text:
state2_security_gate_pass
<-> every_required_category_has_one_outcome
    AND every_APPLICABLE_references_an_accepted_decision
    AND no_UNRESOLVED

Every reference resolves to an indexed item, and every APPLICABLE category
   references at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2.
open_points.question: Must the formal invariant also require every reference to resolve, require the satisfying decision to be indexed, and restrict it to States 0–2, or are those additional test conditions not part of state2_security_gate_pass?
options: Expand the invariant to include all three conditions imposed by Required test 2.
Treat Required test 2 as intentionally stronger than the formal invariant.
Remove the extra conditions from Required test 2.
open_points.default_guess: Expand the formal invariant so its exact pass condition agrees with Required test 2.

witness.initial: A complete review record has no UNRESOLVED category; each required category has one outcome; one APPLICABLE category references accepted decision A16 and also a nonexistent item A999.
events: The workbench evaluates state2_security_gate_pass from the formal invariant.
The workbench runs Required test 2 on the same record.
outcomes: The formal invariant passes because the category references an accepted decision and its other conjuncts hold.
Required test 2 rejects because A999 does not resolve to an indexed item.
witness.observer: The State 3 author sees the security gate alternately open or blocked.

open_points.subject: A21 Required test 2
open_points.text: Every reference resolves to an indexed item
open_points.question: Which occurrences count as a reference: only identifiers in each category's `references:` field, or also identifiers in `affected:`, rationales, witness annotations, and other prose in the review record?
options: Only entries in the structured `references:` field count.
Every item-like identifier anywhere in the complete review record counts.
Entries in `references:` and `affected:` count, but prose and witness annotations do not.
open_points.default_guess: Count only entries in the structured `references:` field.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category has `references: A16` where A16 is indexed and accepted, and `affected: M999` where M999 does not exist.
events: The linter checks the sentence `Every reference resolves to an indexed item`.
outcomes: A linter that treats only `references:` as references accepts the record.
A linter that treats `affected:` identifiers as references rejects the record.
witness.observer: The reviewer sees acceptance or refusal of the same record.

open_points.subject: A21 Required test 2
open_points.question: What index is authoritative, what kinds of State 0–2 items it contains, and what exact evidence makes an item indexed?
options: Only entries in the workbench decision index are indexed items.
Every addressable heading in the State 0–2 documents is an indexed item.
Separate model, decision, and requirement indexes all qualify.
open_points.default_guess: Use one explicit workbench index and reject anything absent from it.

witness.initial: A referenced accepted decision has a heading in a State 0–2 document but no entry in the workbench's decision-index data.
events: The review record names that decision.
outcomes: An implementation that treats document headings as the index accepts the reference.
An implementation that requires a workbench index entry rejects the reference.
witness.observer: The review author sees the same reference pass or fail.

open_points.subject: A21 Required test 2
open_points.question: Which State 0 and State 1 items qualify as accepted decisions, especially accepted `K-*` product passages and `M*` model passages that are not titled `Accepted decision`?
options: Any accepted normative item in States 0–2, including `K-*` and qualifying `M*` items, is an accepted decision.
Only items explicitly titled `Accepted decision` qualify.
Only `A*` decision records qualify, even when other indexed items may be referenced.
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit decision classification in the index rather than inferring it from a `K-*` or `M*` heading.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE authentication category references only K-15, which is an indexed State 0 passage but is not titled `Accepted decision`.
events: The linter checks whether the category references an indexed accepted decision of States 0–2.
outcomes: An implementation that treats accepted State 0 normative passages as decisions accepts the category.
An implementation that recognizes only explicitly classified decision records rejects it.
witness.observer: The security reviewer sees the category pass or fail.

open_points.subject: A21 cross-state reference resolution
open_points.text: references at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2
open_points.question: Are decision identifiers globally unique across States 0–2, state-qualified in references, or rejected when the same unqualified identifier exists in more than one state?
options: Decision identifiers are globally unique across all three states.
References must include the state as well as the decision identifier.
An unqualified identifier resolves by a stated precedence such as State 2 before State 1 before State 0.
Any ambiguous unqualified identifier is refused.
open_points.default_guess: Require state-qualified references and refuse an ambiguous unqualified identifier.

witness.initial: State 0 and State 2 each contain a different indexed accepted decision named A16, and both remain present.
events: An APPLICABLE category records the unqualified reference `A16`.
The workbench resolves the reference and later reports the decision protecting that category.
outcomes: One implementation resolves `A16` to the State 0 decision.
Another resolves `A16` to the State 2 decision.
witness.observer: The reviewer and State 3 author see different security decisions attributed to the category.

open_points.subject: A21 Consequence
open_points.text: State 3 is blocked if any referenced decision is removed or loses its boundary.
open_points.question: For newly permitted references to decisions from States 0 and 1, what exact change counts as a decision losing its boundary, and how is that condition detected?
options: It loses its boundary only when an actor or system boundary named by the decision is removed.
Any scope or applicability change to the decision counts.
A machine-readable boundary identifier must disappear or change.
Only deletion is mechanically checked; `loses its boundary` requires manual review.
open_points.default_guess: Represent boundary coverage explicitly and block only when that machine-readable coverage is removed or changed.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category references an accepted State 0 decision that originally names an agent and the reverse-proxy boundary.
events: The State 0 decision is edited so it still exists and is accepted but no longer names the reverse proxy.
outcomes: An implementation treating removal of any named boundary as `loses its boundary` blocks State 3.
An implementation treating the decision's general scope as unchanged allows State 3.
witness.observer: The State 3 author sees the transition blocked or allowed.
